description: Production-grade knowledge base for Ubuntu kernel tuning, VMware ESXi 7 HP optimization, and Kubernetes node preparation on HPE ProLiant DL360 G8 hardware. Truth-lens nested array architecture. jq_root: '.'

stack.hypervisor: VMware ESXi 7.0 (HPE Custom Image for ProLiant)
stack.hardware: HPE ProLiant DL360 G8 (Intel Xeon E5-26xx v1/v2, Ivy Bridge/Sandy Bridge)

core_principles: {"id": "ESXI_IS_THE_SCHEDULER", "rule": "In a VMware guest, ESXi owns I/O scheduling, CPU scheduling, and memory ballooning. Ubuntu kernel optimizations must NOT compete with the hypervisor; they must defer to it."}

{"id": "PARAVIRTUAL_DRIVERS_MANDATORY", "rule": "All Ubuntu VMs acting as k8s nodes must use VMXNET3 (NIC) and PVSCSI (storage controller). Emulated adapters (E1000, LSI) add CPU overhead and reduce throughput."}

{"id": "SWAP_DISABLED", "rule": "kubelet requires swap to be disabled (enforced since k8s 1.8). ESXi memory ballooning interacts badly with guest swap. Disable swap at both OS and ESXi VM config level."}

{"id": "THP_DISABLED", "rule": "Transparent Huge Pages (THP) must be set to 'never' on k8s nodes. THP causes latency spikes for Redis, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, and Java workloads. ESXi balloon driver conflicts with THP compaction."}

{"id": "CGROUPS_V2_DEFAULT", "rule": "Ubuntu 22.04+ defaults to cgroups v2 (unified hierarchy). Kubernetes 1.25+ fully supports cgroupsv2. Containerd must be configured with SystemdCgroup=true. Do not downgrade to cgroupsv1."}

{"id": "NOOP_IO_SCHEDULER", "rule": "Linux guest on ESXi must use 'none' (noop) I/O scheduler for virtual block devices. ESXi handles all I/O reordering at hypervisor layer. Guest-side scheduling adds double-overhead."}

{"id": "DISK_ENABLE_UUID", "rule": "VM advanced config parameter disk.EnableUUID=TRUE is mandatory for vSphere CSI driver. Without it, VMDK volumes cannot be consistently identified across rescheduling events."}

{"id": "OPEN_VM_TOOLS_REQUIRED", "rule": "open-vm-tools must be installed on every k8s node VM. It provides guest heartbeat, graceful shutdown, time sync, and is required for vCenter to cleanly manage nodes."}

{"id": "NUMA_TOPOLOGY_AWARE", "rule": "DL360 G8 is a dual-socket NUMA system (2x Intel E5-26xx). NUMA node interleaving should be DISABLED in HPE RBSU to preserve NUMA topology visibility. ESXi and guest OS both benefit from local NUMA access."}
{"id": "HARDWARE_VERSION_15_PLUS", "rule": "k8s node VMs must use VMware hardware version 15 or higher to support vSphere CPI/CSI features including hot-add and proper PCI device ID reporting."}

layer_0_hpe_dl360g8_hardware_profile.description: Physical hardware baseline for HPE ProLiant DL360 G8 — the foundation ESXi runs on

truths: DL360 G8 supports 1 or 2x Intel Xeon E5-2600 v1 (Sandy Bridge-EP) or v2 (Ivy Bridge-EP) CPUs
Each socket = 1 NUMA node; dual-socket = 2 NUMA nodes visible to ESXi and guest
E5-2660 v2: 10 cores / 20 threads per socket; max 40 vCPUs total with 2 sockets
Intel VT-x (virtualization), Intel VT-d (IOMMU/directed I/O), and EPT (Extended Page Tables) are supported and must be enabled in RBSU
CPU microcode updates are critical: Spectre/Meltdown patches cause 10-30% performance regression on this generation; mitigations=off acceptable in trusted private-only clusters
DL360 G8 supports up to 768 GB DDR3 ECC RDIMM (24 DIMM slots, 12 per socket/NUMA node)
Optimal memory population: fill all channels symmetrically per NUMA node for maximum bandwidth
HPE RBSU: Node Interleaving must be DISABLED to preserve NUMA awareness; enabling it flattens NUMA into a single UMA domain, hiding topology from ESXi
P420i Smart Array controller on DL360 G8; supports RAID 0/1/5/6/10/50/60
ESXi sees the RAID logical volume as a single VMFS datastore
Local VMFS is acceptable for k8s node OS disks; shared datastore (vSAN, NFS, iSCSI) needed for vSphere CSI PersistentVolumes
SSD-backed datastores dramatically improve etcd performance on control plane nodes
PVSCSI adapter in VM delivers 12% more throughput and 18% less CPU cost vs LSI Logic virtual adapter
DL360 G8 ships with NC375i (4x 1GbE) or NC552i (2x 10GbE) embedded FlexibleLOM
10GbE NICs are strongly preferred for k8s clusters due to pod network traffic amplification
VMXNET3 virtual adapter achieves near line-rate on 10GbE with low CPU overhead via hardware offloads
Separate VMkernel port groups recommended: Management, vMotion, VM Data (k8s)
HP RBSU path: System Configuration > BIOS/Platform Configuration (RBSU)
Power Management: Set to 'Maximum Performance' OR HPE Workload Profile 'Virtualization - Max Performance'
Intel Hyper-Threading: ENABLED (doubles vCPU availability)
Intel Turbo Boost: ENABLED (increases burst clock frequency)
Node Interleaving: DISABLED (preserves NUMA topology)
Intel VT-x: ENABLED; Intel VT-d: ENABLED; Intel TXT: ENABLED
Memory Speed: Maximum Frequency preferred (vs. Power Savings)
Collaborative Power Control: DISABLED when running ESXi (ESXi manages power via its own scheduler)
C-States and P-States: Disable OS control; let BIOS control at 'Maximum Performance' profile
USB 3.0: Can be disabled if not needed (minor improvement to boot time)
QPI Link Power Management: ENABLED at Maximum Performance

layer_1_esxi7_hp_hypervisor_configuratio.description: ESXi 7 host-level settings relevant to Ubuntu k8s node VMs

truths: Use HPE Custom Image for ESXi 7.0 U3 (VMware-ESXi-7.0.3-XXXXXXXX-HPE-703.x.x.x.iso) from HPE Broadcom portal
Custom image includes HPE-specific drivers: HP Smart Array RAID (hpsa), HP NC FlexFabric NICs, AMS (Agentless Management Service), iLO integration
Generic VMware ISO missing HP drivers causes degraded I/O performance and missing iLO health reporting
ESXi 7.0 is the last version officially supporting Gen8 hardware; ESXi 8.0 requires workaround/custom addon
VM Compatibility: ESXi 7.0 U2 or later (hardware version 19)
Guest OS: Ubuntu Linux (64-bit) with correct kernel version selected
SCSI Controller: VMware Paravirtual (PVSCSI) — NOT LSI Logic SAS
Network Adapter: VMXNET3 — NOT E1000 or E1000e
disk.EnableUUID = TRUE in VM Advanced Parameters (required for vSphere CSI)
CPU Hot Add: ENABLED recommended for worker nodes (allows kubelet-managed scaling without full restart)
Memory Hot Add: ENABLED
Latency Sensitivity: 'Normal' for general workloads; 'High' only for real-time pods (requires CPU reservation = limit)
Memory Reservation: Set to 100% of allocated RAM for latency-sensitive nodes (prevents ESXi ballooning)
Do NOT take snapshots of CSI-attached nodes; vSphere CSI behavior with snapshots is undefined
ESXi Power Policy: Set to 'High Performance' via vSphere Client > Host > Manage > Hardware > Power Management
BPDU Filter: Enable on VMkernel ports to prevent spanning-tree loops on pod network VLANs
Promiscuous Mode: Required if using Flannel VXLAN or Calico IPIP — enable on the relevant port group
Forged Transmits: Enable on port group if CNI creates sub-interfaces (Calico, Multus)
MAC Address Changes: Enable if CNI modifies MAC (MetalLB, Multus scenarios)
VMkernel MTU: Set to 9000 (Jumbo Frames) for vMotion and storage VMkernel NICs; ensure physical switch supports jumbo frames
NIC Teaming Policy: Load-based teaming (LBT) preferred over port-based for k8s workloads with many pod connections
ESXi balloon driver (vmmemctl) reclaims guest memory when host is under pressure — causes latency spikes for k8s pods
Prevent ballooning by setting Memory Reservation = Limit (100% reserved) in VM settings for control plane nodes
Transparent Page Sharing (TPS): Disabled by default since ESXi 6.5 for security; do not re-enable
Memory Overcommit: Avoid for k8s clusters; each node should have physical RAM backing equal to its VM allocation
ESXi Swap (.vswp): Ensure fast storage for ESXi swap; control plane nodes should never actually swap
NUMA memory locality: ESXi vNUMA exposes NUMA topology to guest if VM vCPU count > single NUMA node core count
vSphere CPI (cloud-provider-vsphere) version must match Kubernetes minor version: CPI v1.30.x for k8s v1.30
CPI requires vCenter credentials with minimum permissions: read datacenter/datastore/cluster/host, manage VMs
CSI driver requires disk.EnableUUID=TRUE on ALL node VMs (master + workers)
CSI requires VM hardware version >= 15
CPI initializes each node's ProviderID (vsphere://vm-uuid) — CSI uses this to attach VMDK volumes to the correct host
kubeadm init/join must use --cloud-provider=external flag so kubelet does not use built-in cloud provider
All nodes must be tainted with node.cloudprovider.kubernetes.io/uninitialized=true:NoSchedule before CPI deployment; CPI removes taint after initialization
vsphere.conf format changed to YAML in CPI >= 1.2.0; legacy INI format deprecated

layer_2_ubuntu_guest_os_baseline.description: Ubuntu VM configuration steps before kernel tuning — the correct baseline

truths: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (Jammy): Kernel 5.15 HWE (Hardware Enablement); well-tested with k8s; recommended for production
Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (Noble): Kernel 6.8; cgroups v2 default; low-latency features merged into generic kernel; preferred for new clusters
Use Ubuntu Server (no GUI); minimal install reduces attack surface and memory overhead
Install linux-image-generic-hwe-22.04 on 22.04 to get kernel 6.x backport for better VMXNET3 and PVSCSI support
sudo apt install -y open-vm-tools
open-vm-tools replaces VMware Tools ISO — do NOT install both
open-vm-tools provides: guest heartbeat, clean shutdown/reboot, time sync with ESXi host, guest IP reporting to vCenter
Verify running: systemctl status open-vm-tools
VMware Tools status in vCenter should show 'OK (Guest Managed)' after install
For VMs used as templates: install open-vm-tools-deploypkg if using vSphere Site Recovery Manager or linked clones
In VMware guests, timekeeping is managed by the hypervisor; do NOT use NTP independently without coordination
Recommended: Enable VMware Tools time sync (controlled via open-vm-tools) OR use chrony/systemd-timesyncd pointing to reliable NTP
VMware KB 1006427: Guest clock drift is common on overcommitted hosts; use host-based time sync via vmware-tools
For k8s: etcd requires time sync within 500ms across nodes; use consistent NTP source
timedatectl set-ntp true && systemctl enable systemd-timesyncd
Use XFS or ext4 for root and data partitions; XFS preferred for high I/O (better parallelism)
Separate /var/lib/containerd and /var/lib/etcd on dedicated disks/partitions for control plane nodes
Mount options for k8s node data partitions in /etc/fstab: noatime,nodiratime reduces write overhead
If using PVSCSI: disk is presented as /dev/sd* but I/O scheduling must be set to none (noop)
LVM over PVSCSI is acceptable; add noatime to logical volume mount options
Avoid btrfs for k8s nodes; containerd overlay2 driver has known issues with btrfs in some kernel versions
swapoff -a (disable immediately)
Comment out all swap entries in /etc/fstab
If using systemd swap units: systemctl mask swap.target
Verify: swapon --show (must return empty)
kubelet will refuse to start if swap is active and --fail-swap-on=true (default)
Kubernetes 1.28+ added beta SwapMemory feature gate for Linux swap support but it is NOT recommended on ESXi-hosted nodes due to hypervisor memory management conflicts

layer_3_kernel_sysctl_tuning.description: Linux kernel parameter tuning via sysctl for k8s on ESXi. All params go in /etc/sysctl.d/99-k8s-esxi.conf

truths: net.core.somaxconn = 65535  # Max connection backlog; default 128 is too low for k8s API server and pod traffic
net.core.netdev_max_backlog = 65535  # NIC receive queue depth; prevents packet drop under burst
net.core.rmem_max = 134217728  # 128MB max socket receive buffer
net.core.wmem_max = 134217728  # 128MB max socket send buffer
net.core.rmem_default = 31457280  # 30MB default receive buffer
net.core.wmem_default = 31457280  # 30MB default send buffer
net.core.optmem_max = 40960  # Per-socket ancillary buffer size
net.ipv4.tcp_rmem = 4096 87380 134217728  # min/default/max TCP receive buffer
net.ipv4.tcp_wmem = 4096 65536 134217728  # min/default/max TCP send buffer
net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog = 65535  # SYN queue depth; critical for k8s API server under load
net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies = 1  # SYN flood protection; must remain 1
net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse = 1  # Reuse TIME_WAIT sockets; reduces ephemeral port exhaustion in pod-to-pod traffic
net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout = 15  # Reduce TIME_WAIT from 60s default; reclaim ports faster
net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time = 600  # 10min idle before keepalive probes (default 7200s is too long)
net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_intvl = 60  # 60s between probes
net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_probes = 5  # 5 failed probes = connection dead
net.ipv4.tcp_window_scaling = 1  # Enable window scaling for high-bandwidth flows
net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing = 1  # Discover MTU dynamically; important with VMXNET3 and jumbo frames
net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range = 1024 65000  # Expand ephemeral port range for pod traffic
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 1048576  # Connection tracking table size; k8s clusters exhaust default 65536 quickly
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established = 600  # 10min timeout for established connections (vs default 432000s = 5 days)
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_time_wait = 120  # Reduce TIME_WAIT entry lifetime
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_close_wait = 60
Increase hash table buckets: modprobe nf_conntrack hashsize=262144; persist via /etc/modprobe.d/nf_conntrack.conf: options nf_conntrack hashsize=262144
nf_conntrack_max exhaustion manifests as: 'nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet' in dmesg; causes seemingly random pod timeouts
net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables = 1  # Required for most CNI plugins (Flannel, Calico, Weave)
net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-ip6tables = 1  # IPv6 equivalent
net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-arptables = 1  # For ARP bridging
These require br_netfilter kernel module to be loaded BEFORE applying sysctl
modprobe br_netfilter && modprobe overlay  # Add both to /etc/modules-load.d/k8s.conf for persistence
Verify: lsmod | grep br_netfilter
net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1  # MANDATORY for k8s; enables routing between pods across nodes
net.ipv6.conf.all.forwarding = 1  # If using IPv6 CNI
Verify: sysctl net.ipv4.ip_forward  # Should return 1 after applying
vm.swappiness = 0  # Strongly avoid swap; 0 = only swap when absolutely necessary (OOM condition)
vm.dirty_ratio = 20  # % of RAM that can be dirty before sync; increase for write-heavy workloads
vm.dirty_background_ratio = 5  # % of RAM dirty before background writeback starts
vm.dirty_expire_centisecs = 3000  # 30s max dirty page age before forced flush
vm.dirty_writeback_centisecs = 500  # Writeback runs every 5s
vm.overcommit_memory = 1  # Allow memory overcommit; required for many container workloads (Go runtime allocates virtual address space aggressively)
vm.overcommit_ratio = 50  # Limit overcommit to 50% of RAM + swap (when overcommit_memory=2)
vm.max_map_count = 262144  # Required by Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, and other memory-mapped workloads
vm.min_free_kbytes = 131072  # 128MB minimum free; prevents OOM killer thrashing under memory pressure
vm.panic_on_oom = 0  # Do not panic on OOM; let OOM killer handle it
fs.inotify.max_user_watches = 1048576  # Default 8192 is exhausted by Prometheus, Filebeat, and many k8s controllers monitoring thousands of files
fs.inotify.max_user_instances = 8192  # Default 128; increase for many container processes
fs.file-max = 2097152  # System-wide open file descriptor limit
fs.nr_open = 1048576  # Per-process limit
kernel.pid_max = 4194304  # Default 32768; k8s nodes run hundreds of processes; 4M supports high-density clusters
kernel.dmesg_restrict = 0  # Allow non-root to read dmesg; useful for node debugging (restrict in high-security clusters)
kernel.core_uses_pid = 1  # Append PID to core dump filename
kernel.perf_event_paranoid = 3  # Restrict perf events to root; recommended for multi-tenant clusters
kernel.threads-max = 2097152  # Max kernel threads; increase for dense pod environments
net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter = 1  # Reverse path filtering; keep enabled for security
net.ipv4.conf.default.rp_filter = 1
File location: /etc/sysctl.d/99-k8s-esxi.conf
Apply immediately: sysctl --system  OR  sysctl -p /etc/sysctl.d/99-k8s-esxi.conf
Verify a param: sysctl net.core.somaxconn
DaemonSet approach for managed clusters: use initContainer with privileged: true and hostPID: true mounting /proc to apply host-level sysctls
Pod-level sysctls: set in pod.spec.securityContext.sysctls[] for namespaced params (net.core.somaxconn is unsafe/non-namespaced; must be set at node level)

layer_4_kernel_grub_and_boot_params.description: Linux GRUB kernel command line parameters for Ubuntu on ESXi k8s nodes

truths: Add to GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX in /etc/default/grub: transparent_hugepage=never
Also disable defrag: echo never > /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/defrag  (runtime)
Persist via systemd service or rc.local: echo never | tee /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/defrag
GRUB approach is most reliable; survives reboots without additional systemd units
After modifying /etc/default/grub: sudo update-grub && sudo reboot
THP disabled improves latency for Redis, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, Java (JVM), and etcd; no measurable downside for k8s general workloads
Add to GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX: elevator=none  (kernel 5.0+; previously 'noop')
Why: ESXi performs I/O scheduling in the hypervisor; guest scheduler adds latency without benefit
Verify after reboot: cat /sys/block/sda/queue/scheduler  # Should show [none]
For runtime change (no reboot): echo none > /sys/block/sda/queue/scheduler  (replace sda with actual device)
Persist without GRUB: udev rule — SUBSYSTEM=='block', ACTION=='add|change', ATTR{queue/scheduler}='none'  → /etc/udev/rules.d/60-scheduler.rules
NOTE: NVMe devices use mq-deadline by default and perform well; 'none' still works but difference is smaller
Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 default to cgroups v2; verify: stat -fc %T /sys/fs/cgroup/  # Returns 'cgroup2fs'
If cgroupsv1 is detected (older Ubuntu): add systemd.unified_cgroup_hierarchy=1 to GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX
containerd /etc/containerd/config.toml must have: SystemdCgroup = true under [plugins.'io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri'.containerd.runtimes.runc.options]
kubelet KubeletConfiguration must include: cgroupDriver: systemd
Mismatch between kubelet cgroupDriver and containerd SystemdCgroup causes node NotReady and 'cgroup driver' errors in kubelet logs
DL360 G8 Sandy Bridge/Ivy Bridge CPUs are affected by Spectre v1/v2 and Meltdown (L1TF)
Default Ubuntu mitigations impose 10-30% CPU overhead on syscall-heavy workloads (API server, etcd)
For private/trusted networks only: add mitigations=off to GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX to recover performance
Intermediate option: mitigations=auto (applies only necessary mitigations, skips others)
ESXi also applies its own side-channel mitigations via microcode; double-mitigation (ESXi + guest) can be conservative
NEVER disable mitigations on nodes exposed to untrusted tenant workloads
Recommended /etc/default/grub GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX value for ESXi-hosted k8s nodes:
GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="quiet splash elevator=none transparent_hugepage=never cgroup_enable=memory cgroup_enable=cpuset"
For performance-critical private clusters (add): mitigations=off
For NUMA visibility (verify it is already correct): numa=on  (default; only specify if disabled)
Apply: sudo update-grub && sudo reboot
Verify applied: cat /proc/cmdline

layer_5_kubelet_and_containerd_config.description: kubelet and containerd configuration for optimal performance on ESXi-hosted Ubuntu nodes

truths: containerd config default > /etc/containerd/config.toml  (generate fresh default config)
Set SystemdCgroup = true under [plugins.'io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri'.containerd.runtimes.runc.options]
sandbox_image = 'registry.k8s.io/pause:3.9'  (match your k8s version)
Increase containerd ulimits in /etc/systemd/system/containerd.service.d/limits.conf: LimitNOFILE=1048576, LimitNPROC=1048576
containerd storage root: /var/lib/containerd  — place on fast storage, separate partition if possible
overlay2 is default and correct storage driver; DO NOT use devicemapper or aufs on Ubuntu
cgroupDriver: systemd  (must match containerd)
maxPods: 110  (default); increase to 250 on nodes with sufficient resources and raised kernel limits
kubeReserved: cpu='500m', memory='1Gi'  — reserve resources for kubelet and system daemons; prevents OOM eviction of k8s components
systemReserved: cpu='500m', memory='512Mi'
evictionHard: memory.available<200Mi,nodefs.available<10%  — tune based on node RAM
featureGates: MemoryManager=true  — enables NUMA-aware memory allocation for Guaranteed QoS pods
topologyManagerPolicy: single-numa-node  — on dual-socket nodes, pin Guaranteed pods to single NUMA node
cpuManagerPolicy: static  — enables CPU pinning for Guaranteed pods (requests == limits, integer CPUs)
Add to /etc/security/limits.conf (or /etc/security/limits.d/99-k8s.conf):
* soft nofile 1048576
* hard nofile 1048576
* soft nproc 1048576
* hard nproc 1048576
Also set in kubelet.service systemd unit via LimitNOFILE=1048576 LimitNPROC=1048576
Verify effective limits on running kubelet: cat /proc/$(pidof kubelet)/limits
Insufficient file descriptors manifests as: 'too many open files' errors in pod logs and kubelet cannot create inotify watchers

layer_6_node_preparation_sequence.description: Ordered step-by-step node preparation for Ubuntu k8s on ESXi — the correct execution order

truths: 1. VM hardware version >= 15 (19 preferred for ESXi 7)
2. Guest OS: Ubuntu Linux 64-bit
3. SCSI Controller: VMware Paravirtual (PVSCSI)
4. Network Adapter: VMXNET3
5. Advanced Config: disk.EnableUUID = TRUE
6. CPU: allocate cores aligned to NUMA boundary (e.g., 8 or 10 for DL360 G8 10-core socket) for NUMA locality
7. Memory: allocate with reservation = 100% (for control plane and critical nodes)
8. OS Disk: 50-100GB thin provisioned on fast VMFS
9. Additional disk for /var/lib/containerd (control plane: also separate /var/lib/etcd)
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y
sudo apt install -y open-vm-tools curl wget git vim htop iotop sysstat net-tools
sudo hostnamectl set-hostname <node-name>  # unique per node
sudo timedatectl set-ntp true
Disable ufw or configure to allow k8s ports (API server 6443, etcd 2379-2380, kubelet 10250, NodePort 30000-32767)
Create /etc/modules-load.d/k8s.conf with: overlay, br_netfilter, nf_conntrack
modprobe overlay && modprobe br_netfilter && modprobe nf_conntrack
Verify: lsmod | grep -E 'overlay|br_netfilter|nf_conntrack'
nf_conntrack hashsize persistence: echo 'options nf_conntrack hashsize=262144' > /etc/modprobe.d/nf_conntrack.conf
update-initramfs -u  (rebuild initramfs to include modules)
Create /etc/sysctl.d/99-k8s-esxi.conf with all parameters from layer_3
sysctl --system  (apply all sysctl.d files)
Verify critical params: sysctl net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables net.ipv4.ip_forward vm.swappiness fs.inotify.max_user_watches
All should return configured values
swapoff -a
sed -i '/ swap / s/^/#/' /etc/fstab  (comment out swap in fstab)
Edit /etc/default/grub → update GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX
sudo update-grub
sudo reboot  (apply grub changes, test new sysctl, verify swap disabled)
curl -fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg | gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.gpg
echo 'deb [arch=amd64 signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/docker.gpg] https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu $(lsb_release -cs) stable' > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.list
apt install -y containerd.io
containerd config default > /etc/containerd/config.toml
Edit config.toml: set SystemdCgroup = true
systemctl enable --now containerd && systemctl status containerd
curl -fsSL https://pkgs.k8s.io/core:/stable:/v1.30/deb/Release.key | gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/kubernetes-apt-keyring.gpg
echo 'deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/kubernetes-apt-keyring.gpg] https://pkgs.k8s.io/core:/stable:/v1.30/deb/ /' > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kubernetes.list
apt install -y kubelet kubeadm kubectl && apt-mark hold kubelet kubeadm kubectl
systemctl enable kubelet  (kubelet will not start until kubeadm init/join runs)
Ensure all nodes have disk.EnableUUID=TRUE in VM advanced params before kubeadm
kubeadm init must include: --cloud-provider=external (or KubeletConfiguration cloudProvider: external)
After cluster init, verify all nodes tainted: kubectl describe nodes | grep uninitialized
Create vsphere.conf with vCenter credentials and datacenter name
kubectl create configmap cloud-config --from-file=vsphere.conf -n kube-system
Apply CPI manifests matching k8s version from github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider-vsphere/releases
Verify ProviderID set: kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[*].spec.providerID}'  (should show vsphere://vm-uuid for each node)
Apply CSI driver manifests after CPI completes
Verify CSI: kubectl get csidrivers  (csi.vsphere.vmware.com should appear)

layer_7_monitoring_and_diagnostics.description: Commands and tools to verify tuning is applied and diagnose issues on ESXi-hosted k8s nodes

truths: cat /proc/cmdline  # Verify grub params active: elevator=none transparent_hugepage=never
cat /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled  # Should show: always madvise [never]
cat /sys/block/sda/queue/scheduler  # Should show: [none]
swapon --show  # Should return empty
sysctl vm.swappiness  # Should return 0
sysctl net.core.somaxconn  # Should return 65535
sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max  # Should return 1048576
sysctl fs.inotify.max_user_watches  # Should return 1048576
stat -fc %T /sys/fs/cgroup/  # Should return cgroup2fs (cgroupsv2)
systemctl status open-vm-tools  # Should be active (running)
vmstat -s  # Memory usage overview; check swap used (should be 0)
iostat -xz 1 5  # I/O stats per device; %util should not be near 100% for PVSCSI devices
ss -s  # Socket stats; watch for large TIME_WAIT counts indicating tcp_tw_reuse not working
cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack | wc -l  # Compare against nf_conntrack_max; should be <80% of max
dmesg | grep -i 'nf_conntrack\|table full'  # Connection tracking overflow indicator
dmesg | grep -i 'oom\|out of memory'  # OOM events
journalctl -u kubelet --since '1 hour ago'  # kubelet errors
kubectl describe node <name>  # Check Conditions, Allocatable, Events
kubectl top nodes  # Real-time resource usage (requires metrics-server)
kubectl get nodes -o wide  # Verify all nodes Ready with correct IPs
kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}: {.spec.providerID}{"\n"}{end}'  # ProviderID check
kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l app=vsphere-cloud-controller-manager  # CPI pods running
kubectl -n vmware-system-csi get pods  # CSI pods running (vsphere-csi-controller, vsphere-csi-node DaemonSet)
kubectl describe csinodes  # Shows attached volumes per node
kubectl get events -n kube-system --field-selector reason=ProviderError  # vSphere API errors
On ESXi: esxcli vm process list  # Verify VM is running; check memory balloon: esxcli vm process stats -w <worldID>

layer_8_common_pitfalls.description: Known failure modes and their root causes + fixes for this exact stack

truths: PITFALL: kubelet fails to start with 'swap memory is not disabled' — FIX: swapoff -a + comment /etc/fstab swap entries + verify no systemd swap units
PITFALL: Pods fail with 'nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet' — FIX: increase net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max to 1048576 and hashsize to 262144
PITFALL: inotify watch exhaustion, Prometheus/Filebeat silently stops monitoring — FIX: fs.inotify.max_user_watches=1048576
PITFALL: vSphere CSI cannot attach VMDK; PVC stuck in Pending — FIX: verify disk.EnableUUID=TRUE on ALL node VMs (restart VM after setting)
PITFALL: CPI never initializes nodes (taint never removed); pods stuck — FIX: verify kubeadm was run with --cloud-provider=external; check CPI pod logs; check vsphere.conf credentials
PITFALL: Node shows incorrect/missing ProviderID — FIX: CPI not running or vsphere.conf datacenter path wrong; must match exact vCenter datacenter object name
PITFALL: containerd fails to start, cgroupDriver mismatch — FIX: ensure SystemdCgroup=true in containerd config.toml AND cgroupDriver: systemd in kubelet config

PITFALL: Bridge traffic not going through iptables, pod networking broken — FIX: modprobe br_netfilter + net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables=1 + net.ipv4.ip_forward=1; confirm module loads on boot via /etc/modules-load.d/k8s.conf
PITFALL: High latency spikes on Redis/Postgres pods — FIX: disable THP (transparent_hugepage=never in grub + systemd unit); verify no THP compaction running: grep AnonHugePages /proc/meminfo

PITFALL: Guest clock drift, etcd leader elections, certificate expiry warnings — FIX: ensure open-vm-tools is running and time sync enabled; or configure chrony against reliable NTP synchronized with ESXi host
PITFALL: VMXNET3 packet loss under high pod traffic — FIX: increase net.core.netdev_max_backlog to 65535; check ESXi port group for TX/RX errors in vSphere client

PITFALL: ESXi balloon driver inflating inside k8s nodes causing OOM kills — FIX: set Memory Reservation = Allocation in VM settings for control plane nodes; do not overcommit memory at ESXi host level for k8s clusters

PITFALL: Using generic ESXi ISO instead of HPE Custom Image — FIX: HP Smart Array P420i may work but miss optimized drivers; ILO health reporting broken; use HPE Custom Image for ESXi 7.0 U3 (July 2022 or later)

PITFALL: Node interleaving enabled in RBSU, ESXi shows single NUMA node — FIX: disable Node Interleaving in HPE RBSU; ESXi then exposes 2 NUMA nodes; kubelet topology manager can pin Guaranteed pods to single NUMA node
PITFALL: CSI hot-add volume attachment fails — FIX: VM must have CPU and Memory Hot Add enabled; PVSCSI supports hot-add disk without VM restart; LSI controller does NOT

content: # K8s on VMware ESXi Ubuntu Node Tuning

grub_cmdline_recommendation.description: Recommended GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX in /etc/default/grub for ESXi-hosted k8s nodes
grub_cmdline_recommendation.standard: GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="quiet splash elevator=none transparent_hugepage=never cgroup_enable=memory cgroup_enable=cpuset"
grub_cmdline_recommendation.performance_private_cluster: GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="quiet splash elevator=none transparent_hugepage=never cgroup_enable=memory cgroup_enable=cpuset mitigations=off"

modules_load_k8s_conf.description: /etc/modules-load.d/k8s.conf — kernel modules to load at boot

vsphere_conf_template.description: vsphere.conf template for CPI (YAML format, CPI >= 1.2.0)

vm_advanced_params.description: VMware VM Advanced Configuration Parameters required for k8s

anti_patterns.pattern: Using E1000/E1000e network adapter for k8s nodes
anti_patterns.cause: Emulated Intel NIC; all network operations go through CPU emulation
anti_patterns.fix: Switch to VMXNET3; Ubuntu includes the driver natively

anti_patterns.pattern: Using LSI Logic SCSI controller instead of PVSCSI
anti_patterns.cause: LSI is emulated; higher CPU overhead, lower throughput for disk-heavy workloads (etcd, containerd image pulls)
anti_patterns.fix: Use VMware Paravirtual (PVSCSI) controller; supports boot disk since ESXi 4.1+

anti_patterns.pattern: Not setting disk.EnableUUID=TRUE before deploying k8s
anti_patterns.cause: vSphere CSI driver cannot identify VMDK volumes without consistent UUID
anti_patterns.fix: Set in VM Advanced Parameters; requires VM power cycle to take effect; must be done BEFORE kubeadm init

anti_patterns.pattern: Leaving swap enabled on k8s nodes
anti_patterns.cause: kubelet enforces --fail-swap-on=true by default; swap and ESXi balloon driver interact unpredictably
anti_patterns.fix: swapoff -a; comment /etc/fstab swap entries; mask systemd swap units

anti_patterns.cause: kubelet uses deprecated in-tree vSphere provider or no provider; CPI cannot set ProviderID; CSI volumes cannot attach
anti_patterns.fix: Pass --cloud-provider=external to kubeadm init/join or set in KubeletConfiguration

anti_patterns.pattern: Not loading br_netfilter before applying bridge sysctl params
anti_patterns.cause: sysctl apply succeeds but bridge-nf-call-iptables is silently ignored without the module; pod networking broken
anti_patterns.fix: modprobe br_netfilter before sysctl --system; add to /etc/modules-load.d/k8s.conf

anti_patterns.pattern: Leaving THP enabled on k8s nodes
anti_patterns.cause: THP compaction causes latency spikes; conflicts with ESXi balloon driver; Redis/MongoDB/etcd warn about this explicitly

anti_patterns.pattern: Using generic VMware ESXi ISO on HPE ProLiant DL360 G8
anti_patterns.cause: Missing HPE-specific drivers for P420i Smart Array, NC FlexLOM NICs, iLO integration, and AMS health monitoring
anti_patterns.fix: Use HPE Custom Image for ESXi 7.0 U3 (July 2022+ release); download from Broadcom/HPE customer portal

anti_patterns.pattern: Enabling Node Interleaving in HPE RBSU with ESXi
anti_patterns.cause: Node Interleaving flattens NUMA topology into a single UMA domain; ESXi loses NUMA awareness; vCPU scheduling suboptimal
anti_patterns.fix: DISABLE Node Interleaving in RBSU; NUMA is ENABLED by disabling interleaving on HP servers (counterintuitive)

anti_patterns.pattern: Setting cgroupDriver: cgroupfs in kubelet while containerd uses SystemdCgroup=true
anti_patterns.cause: cgroup driver mismatch causes node NotReady and container creation failures
anti_patterns.fix: Both must use systemd: cgroupDriver: systemd in kubelet config AND SystemdCgroup=true in containerd config.toml

anti_patterns.pattern: Taking snapshots of VMs running as vSphere CSI nodes
anti_patterns.cause: vSphere CSI documentation explicitly warns snapshots of CNS node VMs cause errors and unpredictable behavior
anti_patterns.fix: Use Velero with vSphere CSI snapshots API for k8s-level backups; do not use vSphere snapshots on k8s nodes

anti_patterns.pattern: Overcommitting memory at ESXi host level for k8s nodes
anti_patterns.cause: ESXi balloon driver inflates inside guest VMs to reclaim memory; causes guest kernel to swap; violates k8s swap=disabled guarantee
anti_patterns.fix: Set Memory Reservation = Limit (100%) for control plane VMs; avoid memory overcommit ratio >1.0 on hosts running k8s nodes

anti_patterns.pattern: Using default nf_conntrack_max (65536) for k8s nodes
anti_patterns.cause: k8s clusters with 50+ pods easily exhaust 65536 tracked connections; manifests as random packet drops and connection resets

anti_patterns.pattern: Leaving default fs.inotify.max_user_watches (8192) on k8s nodes
anti_patterns.cause: Prometheus node-exporter, Filebeat, kubelets watching pod directories, and VS Code server each consume hundreds of inotify watches; default exhausted instantly

anti_patterns.pattern: Using CFQ/BFQ I/O scheduler for block devices in ESXi guest
anti_patterns.cause: ESXi already performs I/O reordering at hypervisor layer; guest-side scheduler adds latency without benefit; double scheduling
anti_patterns.fix: elevator=none in GRUB or echo none > /sys/block/sda/queue/scheduler
